article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Indica / 40% Sativa
Genetics: California Hash Plant × Blueberry
Breeder: Dinafem Seeds
THC Content: 12–16%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Hash, earth, sweet berries, blueberry
Flowering Time (Indoor): 50–55 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: 475 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 1,100 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

Blue Hash was designed around a problem that eliminates many otherwise excellent cannabis strains from outdoor gardens: difficult weather. Cold nights, damp autumns, and mountainous conditions can turn dense indica flowers into a liability, yet Dinafem deliberately selected this cultivar to remain productive where less resilient marijuana may struggle. California Hash Plant supplies the hardy, resin-heavy Afghan character, while Blueberry introduces sweet fruit, distinctive pigmentation, and a softer aromatic dimension. The finished plant is compact and sturdy indoors but capable of reaching roughly three meters outside, giving growers considerable control over its final size.

Its name describes the strain unusually well. Resin production is substantial enough to make the flowers attractive for traditional hash and other concentrates, while cooler nighttime temperatures can bring out striking violet and purple tones inherited from the Blueberry side. The sensory profile avoids modern candy and dessert excess in favor of wet earth, sweet berries, and a deep hash-like aroma. Combined with a rapid 50–55-day bloom and an unmistakably relaxing effect, Blue Hash offers an old-school form of cannabis that remains practical even for growers dealing with relatively hostile climates.
Genetics and Lineage

Dinafem created Blue Hash by crossing California Hash Plant with Blueberry. The California Hash Plant parent provides much of the cultivar’s durability and traditional indica structure. Dinafem’s version of California Hash Plant was itself developed through a highly indica-dominant line involving Hash Plant and Northern Light , with selection focused heavily on rapid flowering, dense resin, compact branching, and the ability to cope with cold and humid environments. Those traits transfer directly into Blue Hash, particularly its sturdy architecture and unusually strong performance under outdoor conditions that would challenge many dense-flowered indicas.

Blueberry contributes an entirely different set of qualities. The famous Blue family traces back to DJ Short ‘s work combining tropical sativa ancestry, including Purple Thai-related genetics, with Afghan indica. That breeding produced cultivars celebrated for berry sweetness, colorful foliage and flowers, resin, and a more nuanced experience than a purely sedating Afghan line. The purple and violet pigmentation that can appear in Blue Hash when nighttime temperatures fall is one of the most obvious expressions of that ancestry.

Together, the parents create a 60% indica and 40% sativa hybrid rather than an extreme broad-leaf plant. California Hash Plant establishes the compact buds, quick maturation, resin, and physical calm, while Blueberry adds fruit, color, and enough hybrid influence to keep the cultivar from feeling completely one-dimensional. The cross also preserves the hash-making potential of its Afghan-oriented parent while producing a sweeter finished flower, which is central to the strain’s appeal.
Effects and Experience

Blue Hash moves quickly toward physical relaxation. Instead of beginning with a prolonged cerebral rush, the body tends to register the effects early, with muscular tension giving way to a heavier, calmer sensation. The overall pace of the experience slows, yet the strain does not necessarily produce immediate sleepiness at a moderate serving. There can be a comfortable mental ease alongside the physical calm, making quiet conversation, music, movies, or an unhurried evening feel particularly natural.

As the dose rises, the indica character becomes substantially more obvious. Limbs can feel heavier, motivation to remain active declines, and the experience may become deeply restful. Dinafem characterized the effect as powerful, relaxing, and long lasting, which is notable because the breeder-listed THC range of 12–16% appears modest beside many modern strains. Blue Hash illustrates why cannabinoid percentage alone does not fully describe the character or perceived strength of marijuana.

Consumers accustomed to contemporary flower testing above 25% THC should not automatically assume this cultivar will feel weak. Its concentrated body effect can be substantial, particularly for people with lower tolerance. Excessive consumption may cause dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, lethargy, or temporary mental fog. A moderate serving better preserves the pleasant balance between physical relief and a calm but usable headspace.
Medical Benefits

The strong physical component may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer body relaxation over pronounced cerebral stimulation. Muscular tightness and everyday physical discomfort may become less intrusive as the heavier stage develops, while the calmer mental tone can make it easier to disengage from stress at the end of the day. Its comparatively moderate THC specification may also interest people who do not deliberately seek the highest-potency flower available, although individual response can still vary significantly.

Appetite stimulation is another characteristic historically associated with this strain, and larger servings may encourage both eating and rest. The same heavy relaxation can make evening use more practical than situations requiring sustained coordination, driving, or demanding concentration. Some consumers may also find the later stages useful as part of a nighttime routine because the experience becomes increasingly quiet and physically settled.

Blue Hash should not be treated as a guaranteed treatment for pain, appetite problems, sleep difficulties, or any other condition. Dinafem lists low CBD, meaning the cultivar remains primarily THC-driven despite its moderate cannabinoid range. Medical users should consider the tested potency of the actual batch, personal tolerance, medications, and their previous reaction to indica-dominant marijuana rather than relying solely on the strain’s reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Hash defines the aromatic foundation. The scent has the dry, resinous depth associated with traditional Afghan cannabis, accompanied by earth that can resemble damp soil or freshly turned forest ground. This is not the sharp petroleum profile of modern gas genetics; the heaviness feels warmer and more organic, giving the flower an unmistakably old-school quality.

Blueberry genetics soften that foundation with sweet berries. The fruit is usually more noticeable once the flowers are broken apart or during the exhale, where the heavier hash and earth give way to a smoother sweetness. Some plants can lean toward blueberry, while others keep the berry character more generalized. Cooler finishing temperatures may intensify pigmentation, but color itself does not guarantee a stronger fruit aroma.

When smoked, the flavor typically begins earthy and resinous before revealing a sweeter berry finish. Vaporization can make the fruit portion more apparent because the delicate aromatic compounds are preserved at lower temperatures. Proper drying and curing are especially useful with this cultivar: rushing the process can leave the flower tasting mostly earthy, while a controlled cure allows the contrast between Afghan hash and sweet Blueberry ancestry to become much clearer.
Growing Information

Blue Hash is one of Dinafem’s more forgiving outdoor-oriented cultivars. Plants develop dense, sturdy frames with jagged leaves and can be kept relatively compact indoors by controlling container size and vegetative time. Outdoors, unrestricted roots and a long season can produce plants approaching three meters. The breeder specifically selected the strain for resistance to cold and moisture, making it unusually adaptable for an indica-dominant cultivar with compact flowers. That resilience is one of its strongest advantages for growers in mountainous, northern, or generally unpredictable climates.

Indoor flowering takes only 50–55 days, with Dinafem listing production around 475 g/m² under suitable conditions. The plant is not considered especially hungry, so aggressive feeding is unnecessary; a balanced nutrient program is generally sufficient. Dense, compact buds accumulate a substantial trichome layer as harvest approaches, making the crop particularly useful for dry sift, hash, and other resin preparations. Cooler nighttime temperatures can trigger vivid purple and violet coloration, especially when the difference between day and night temperatures becomes pronounced.

Outdoor plants finish from early to mid-October and can produce up to approximately 1,100 grams each under excellent conditions. Although the genetics cope better with moisture than many indicas, resistance should not be mistaken for immunity to mold. Good spacing, airflow, well-drained soil, and regular inspection remain worthwhile when autumn weather turns wet. For novice growers, the combination of simple feeding requirements, fast flowering, climate tolerance, and strong production makes Blue Hash considerably more approachable than its exotic appearance might imply.
FAQ
What strains make Blue Hash?

Blue Hash was bred by Dinafem Seeds from California Hash Plant × Blueberry. California Hash Plant contributes hardy Afghan-oriented indica traits and heavy resin, while Blueberry adds sweet berry flavors and colorful pigmentation.
Is Blue Hash indica or sativa?
Blue Hash is approximately 60% indica and 40% sativa. Its effects and flower structure lean toward the indica side, with pronounced physical relaxation, dense buds, and a short flowering period.
How much THC does Blue Hash have?
Dinafem lists Blue Hash at approximately 12–16% THC with low CBD. Actual cannabinoid content can vary according to cultivation conditions, phenotype, harvest maturity, and testing methodology.
What does Blue Hash taste like?
The primary flavors are traditional hash, earth, and sweet berries. Blueberry-like sweetness becomes particularly noticeable on the finish, balancing the heavier Afghan-style resin and earthy notes.
How long does Blue Hash take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately 50–55 days. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity from early to mid-October in Northern Hemisphere gardens.
Final Thoughts on Blue Hash

Blue Hash stands apart from many colorful cannabis strains because its purple appearance is only one part of a much broader breeding purpose. Dinafem combined California Hash Plant and Blueberry to produce weed capable of handling cold and damp conditions while still delivering dense flowers, heavy resin, attractive pigmentation, and a flavorful harvest. The emphasis on resilience makes the cultivar especially noteworthy among traditional indica-dominant hybrids.

Its garden performance remains impressive even by modern standards. A 50–55-day flowering cycle is exceptionally convenient, while breeder figures of roughly 475 g/m² indoors and up to 1,100 grams per plant outdoors give the strain serious production potential. Easy feeding requirements and tolerance for challenging weather broaden its appeal further, particularly for outdoor growers who cannot rely on a long, dry autumn.

The finished flower brings the entire pedigree together. Earthy Afghan hash forms the base, berries add sweetness, and a strong body-centered effect provides the classic relaxing character expected from its name. For growers and consumers interested in old-school marijuana genetics, colorful Blueberry influence, and genuine hash-making potential rather than fashionable dessert flavors, Blue Hash remains one of Dinafem’s most distinctive indica-oriented creations.
